edges.description: Injury may establish an inflammatory repair environment; human atlas timing does not prove that the measured niche precedes adhesion formation.
Injury can reduce epithelial coverage, but the human atlas does not trace the time course or prove universal stem-cell depletion.
Some injuries heal with scar rather than complete regeneration; multiple cellular intermediates remain unresolved.
An inflammatory niche may favor a fibrogenic stromal state; the cross-sectional atlas does not establish a specific cytokine as necessary.
Reduced epithelial coverage may limit the functional implantation surface; cell abundance and clinical receptivity were not experimentally separated.
Loss of functioning endometrial surface may reduce menstrual shedding, independently of obstruction.
Severe loss of functioning endometrium may prevent menstrual shedding; endocrine and outflow causes require separate assessment.
Altered WNT communication may contribute to impaired epithelial differentiation and receptivity; composition, hormone exposure and causality are unresolved.
A differentiation-related contribution is proposed; no intervention isolates NOTCH as the cause of human infertility.
DIO2 knockdown is associated with increased ERK phosphorylation in culture; the intervening mechanism is unresolved.
MEK-pathway inhibition reduces the MTOR-associated phosphorylation state after DIO2 knockdown, supporting indirect pathway involvement.
MTOR-associated signaling is proposed to suppress autophagy in this experimental context; no selective ATG genetic epistasis establishes the complete route.
Chloroquine and rapamycin oppositely modify EMT-associated markers; drug pleiotropy and non-autophagic effects remain possible.
Erastin causes EMT-associated marker changes in epithelial preparations; this does not establish all injury-associated EMT as ferroptosis-dependent.
Supernatant from erastin-stimulated epithelial cells carries fibrogenic activity; the responsible mediator remains unidentified in the accessible source.
The culture transfer experiment supports stromal response to epithelial supernatant without identifying the necessary secreted factor.
Fibrogenic stromal activity can contribute to excess matrix; the relative human cellular sources and mediators remain unresolved.
An endothelial contribution is a model-derived hypothesis based on co-localized markers accompanying fibrosis, not proven lineage-mediated matrix production.
Fibrous tissue can bridge opposing endometrial surfaces and distort the cavity.
Replacement of functional endometrium can reduce suitable implantation surface, with additional functional and fertility factors remaining relevant.
Prior endometrial scarring may disrupt the maternal placental interface; post-adhesiolysis cohort associations do not isolate this mechanism or prove that treatment itself is the sole cause.
The pathological bands correspond to the observed defining lesion.
Adhesions involving the outflow tract may obstruct menstrual drainage; not every adhesion produces obstruction.
Cavity distortion or ostial obstruction may impede reproduction, alongside endometrial and unrelated fertility factors.
Partial obstruction may reduce external menstrual flow.
Complete outflow obstruction can prevent external bleeding.
Trapped cycling menstrual effluent can produce recurrent pain.
Outflow blockage may retain menstrual blood; it is not a universal manifestation.
Retrograde menstruation is a proposed possible contributor to coexisting endometriosis, without a demonstrated disease-wide risk.
A deficient implantation environment may contribute to infertility; this is a clinical inference rather than pathway-specific causal proof.
Abnormal residual endometrium may contribute to pregnancy loss after implantation; infertility and miscarriage are distinct endpoints with multiple possible causes.
DIO2 si-1 reduces DIO2 RNA and protein.
DIO2 knockdown increases MAPK/ERK phosphorylation.
Chloroquine removes the marker benefit associated with DIO2 overexpression.
T3 increases autophagic turnover in the lysosomal-blockade comparison.

Supernatant carries transferable fibrogenic activity.
HESC fibrotic response increases after stimulated epithelial supernatant.
CD31 and alpha-SMA double-positive cells are observed after injury.
